Belarusian

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • rod — Łacinka (Belarusian Latin alphabet)

Etymology

[edit]

From Old Ruthenian родъ (rod), from Old East Slavic родъ (rodŭ), from Proto-Slavic *rodъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *radás.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [rot]
  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

род • (rod) m inan (genitive ро́ду, nominative plural ро́ды, genitive plural ро́даў)

  1. (grammar) gender
  2. (taxonomy) genus

Bulgarian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *rodъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *radás.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [rɔt]
  • Audio (Standard Bulgarian):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɔt

Noun

[edit]

род • (rod) m

  1. tribe
  2. family, kin
  3. (grammar) gender
  4. (taxonomy) genus

[edit]
verbs
  • роде́я се impf (rodéja se)
  • родя́ pf (rodjá, “to give birth”)
nouns
  • и́зрод (ízrod)
  • наро́д (naród)
  • срод (srod)

    • родолю́бие (rodoljúbie, “patriotism”), родолю́бив (rodoljúbiv)
    • родонача́лник m (rodonačálnik), родонача́лница f (rodonačálnica, “ancestor”)
    • родооснова́тел (rodoosnovátel, “family founder”)
    • родоотстъ́пник (rodootstǎ́pnik, “apostate”)

    • родозащи́тник (rodozaštítnik, “protector of one's kin”)
adjectives

  • ро́дов (ródov)
  • родови́т (rodovít)

Macedonian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *rodъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *radás.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [rɔt]

Noun

[edit]

род • (rod) m (plural родови, relational adjective родов)

  1. tribe, family
  2. race, kind, sort
  3. fruit
  4. gender (social & grammatical)

Declension

[edit]
Declension of род
singular plural
indefinite род (rod) родови (rodovi)
definite unspecified родот (rodot) родовите (rodovite)
definite proximal родов (rodov) родовиве (rodovive)
definite distal родон (rodon) родовине (rodovine)
vocative роду (rodu) родови (rodovi)
count form — рода (roda)

Derived terms

[edit]
  • изрод (izrod)

Russian

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • родъ (rod) — pre-1918 spelling

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old East Slavic родъ (rodŭ), from Proto-Slavic *rodъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *radás. Maybe from Proto-Indo-European *wréh₂ds (“root”), whence English root. Cognates include Latvian rads, Ukrainian рід (rid) and Polish ród amongst others.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [rot]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (Saint Petersburg):(file)
  • Homophone: рот (rot)
  • Rhymes: -ot

Noun

[edit]

род • (rod) m inan (genitive ро́да, nominative plural роды́, genitive plural родо́в, relational adjective родово́й)

  1. generation, birth, origin, stock, family, race, tribe, lineage
    о́т роду ― ót rodu ― of age

Serbo-Croatian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *rodъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *radás.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /rôːd/

Noun

[edit]

ро̑д m inan (Latin spelling rȏd)

  1. gender
  2. (botany) genus
  3. relative, relation
  4. fruit, crop, extraction (rarely used in these senses)
  5. family, stock, lineage, kin, race
    • 1872, “Bože pravde”, Jovan Đorđević (lyrics), Davorin Jenko (music):
      Боже спаси, Боже храни / Српског краља, српски род!
      God, our hope: Protect and cherish / The Serbian king and Serbian race!

Declension

[edit]
Declension of род

vocative роде родови
locative роду родовима
instrumental родом родовима

  • на́род
  • по̀род

  • ро̀довскӣ
